fig1_rabi_oscillations.svg: Semiclassical Rabi flopping $P_e(t)=(\Omega^2/\Omega_R^2)\sin^2(\Omega_R t/2)$ from rabi_excited_population for detunings $\delta=0,\Omega,2\Omega$. On resonance the atom fully inverts every $\Omega t=\pi$ ($\pi$-pulse) and returns at $2\pi$; off resonance the flop is faster ($\Omega_R=\sqrt{\Omega^2+\delta^2}$) but saturates at $\Omega^2/(\Omega^2+\delta^2)<1$ (dotted lines). Open circles are a genuine $e^{-iHt}|g\rangle$ evolution under two_level_hamiltonian, matching the closed form.
fig2_collapse_revival.svg: Atomic inversion $\langle\sigma_z\rangle(t)$ for an excited atom over a coherent field ($\bar n=|\alpha|^2=16$, resonant) from jcm_inversion (solid). Field quantization replaces the single Rabi tone by a Poisson sum of tones $2g\sqrt{n+1}$: they dephase, so the inversion COLLAPSES to zero on $t_c\sim\sqrt{2}/g$, then rephase into a partial REVIVAL near $t_r\sim2\pi\sqrt{\bar n}/g$ -- with no classical-field counterpart. Open circles are the independent closed-form Poisson sum (resonant_inversion_series).
